name: Redwood Research (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: an AI catastrophe kills people everywhere and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population.
summary: Redwood Research (Berkeley) researches AI that works against its developers: it started AI control (keeping a model safe to use even if it tries to subvert its monitors), showed with Anthropic that a production model can fake alignment, and advises AI companies and the UK AI Security Institute. This model covers its one programme in 2024 ($2.9M spent), its own research and a $0.68M grant that completed the spin-off of the Constellation research centre. At the defaults it averts about 0.26 years of healthy life per $1,000, from 0.006 to 12 on the combined range, so the result is mostly uncertainty: each dollar is valued as a typical project's cut in the forecast risk of an AI catastrophe (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model, the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament's experts), deaths valued like every death and the future lost counted through the discount rate. It is about a third of FAR.AI's, because nearly all its work is on misaligned AI (5% against misuse, against FAR.AI's 28%; Rethink's typical misuse project cuts far more deaths per dollar), and four times MIRI's mostly because of that 5%: with none it would be about 0.05, close to MIRI's. The next dollar counts at a third of the past average because 2024 ran on over two years of reserves. The chance of an AI catastrophe (the slider), the misuse cut and the years a cut counts are the biggest swings; the one branch is discounted for missing data: no outcome of the work on the risk is measured.

rows.label: AI: share of the AI spending on work against misuse (dangerous-capability evaluations, defences against misuse)
rows.explainer: The share of Redwood's AI spending that is work against misuse. Its research is on AI that works against its developers: AI control (protocols that stay safe if a model is trying to subvert them), alignment faking, hidden reasoning. Of its four 2024 outputs on its research page (password-locked models, alignment faking, adaptive deployment of untrusted models, the control safety case), only the password-locked models paper also serves misuse work, by showing how to elicit capabilities a model hides in dangerous-capability evaluations; it serves evaluations of scheming models as much. About a fifth of that paper's share, 5%, our judgment, 0 to 15% (the paper's share at most); work aimed at both counts as misalignment. Below FAR.AI's 28% and the Center for AI Safety's 25%, which run jailbreak and hazardous-knowledge work; MIRI's is 0.

Own research spending in 2024
rows.explainer: Redwood's own research: the programme expenses less the Constellation grant. In 2024: AI control (adaptive deployment of untrusted models; the control safety case with the UK AI Security Institute), alignment faking with Anthropic, capability elicitation with password-locked models (NeurIPS 2024), and advice to AI companies; six employees (Part V line 2a), compute and model access (DigitalOcean, Lambda, OpenAI: $623,121, Part VII section B) and contractors.

rows.explainer: Constellation, the Berkeley AI safety research centre Redwood started and ran until 2023, became its own charity: Redwood passed on a $250,000 grant it held for it and the office's leasehold improvements ($429,955 at fair value), for general support. The grant buys the centre's work (desks, visiting researchers, fellowships), valued like the field's typical dollar, discounted in grant_evidence_adj; it isn't money moved to a modelled charity (Constellation has no model).

rows.label: Research: how far the typical project's effect applies
rows.explainer: Redwood's research against Rethink Priorities' typical small AI project. Above typical: it started AI control as a field ('AI companies and other researchers have since built on this work', its home page says), it advises Google DeepMind and Anthropic on misaligned-AI risk, its alignment-faking study with Anthropic showed a production model (Claude 3 Opus) faking alignment in training, and it wrote a control safety case with the UK AI Security Institute, so its outputs go straight into how developers and a government institute test models. Below in how directly it acts: a protocol cuts the risk only once labs use it on their most capable models. 1.2, our judgment, 0.5 to 2.5, as for FAR.AI's and the Center for AI Safety's research (1.2), the family's upper bound for a typical dollar; the low end higher than theirs (0.4) for the direct uptake into labs' and a government's safety methods, the range wide because no lab says which protocols it runs.

rows.explainer: How far Rethink Priorities' typical small AI project applies to Redwood's work: its research and the Constellation grant weighted by spending: about 1.05.

rows.label: Share of the work no one else would have done now
rows.explainer: The share of the work no one else would have done now: Redwood proposed AI control and is still its main independent group; labs' own teams (Anthropic's alignment stress-testing team co-wrote alignment faking) and the UK AI Security Institute now work on control too, partly because of it, and would have done some of this work anyway. Our judgment, 0.7 (0.4 to 0.9), between FAR.AI's 0.65 and MIRI's 0.75; that the work would have come later is in years_of_impact.

rows.label: Research: Redwood's share of the resources from people and groups it doesn't pay
rows.explainer: Outside resources behind the research evidence_adj is judged on: alignment faking had 20 authors, three of them Redwood's (Greenblatt, Roger, Shlegeris) and most of the rest Anthropic's, with Anthropic's models and compute; the control safety case was written with the UK AI Security Institute; outside scholars' time. Redwood's people led the work (Greenblatt is first author). 0.65, our judgment, 0.45 to 0.9, below FAR.AI's and MIRI's 0.85 because its largest 2024 result was a joint project with a lab.

rows.explainer: Redwood is funded almost wholly by Open Philanthropy, now Coefficient Giving (general support grants of 2021 to 2023 and a $1.1M grant for collaborations with outside researchers in 2025), which fills gaps actively, so it may give less if small donors give more: 0.8 (0.55 to 1.05), our judgment, a little below FAR.AI's and the Center for AI Safety's 0.85, which have several large funders.

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the catastrophes counted: control also guards against harms smaller than a catastrophe (an AI agent's sabotage or data theft inside a lab), and Redwood's researchers mentor outside scholars (MATS) and write much of the public strategy on control. 10% (0 to 30%) of the modelled value, our judgment, as for FAR.AI and the Center for AI Safety.

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire (in the shared cut): control is meant to make it safe to use models that may be misaligned, so it can also let labs deploy more capable models sooner, or feel safe doing so. -5%, our judgment, down to -20%, as for the Center for AI Safety's -5%, above FAR.AI's -3% because the speed-up is control's stated use.
